riskBefore: Docker/UAT RFC1918 peers were rejected, encouraging broad SSRF exceptions or unusable route contacts.
controlsAdded: Immutable startup-built allowlist keyed by recipient router ID, canonical literal RFC1918 IPv4 /32, port, and exact path.
Same policy instance used for route contact eligibility and actual socket address selection.
Production environment and mainnet/test-identity startup guards.
Private hostname and public-to-private DNS rebinding denial at connect time.
Loopback, link-local/cloud metadata, multicast, unspecified, shared, documentation, IPv6 private, redirects, and proxies remain blocked.
residualRisks: UAT operators must protect configuration integrity and stable container address assignment.
The allowlist permits direct HTTP to explicitly named RFC1918 peers; confidentiality still depends on the existing signed onion envelope and trusted UAT host/network boundary.
A compromised router identity already present in the UAT allowlist can receive traffic addressed to that identity.
